title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: The equation label reads (155), with (152) crossed out. Since the preceding display is (144) and the next page continues with (146), it should almost certainly be (145): a numbering slip.

The non-triviality of the extension is not proved on this page. It is reduced to the extension M(0)^~, whose non-triviality is said (next page) to have been established 'plus haut'. That cannot be checked from this page.
The cartesian property of squares I–III is asserted as following from diagram (144) without detail. It is plausible, since all vertical maps are index-2 μ-extensions compatible with the maps.

ideas.what: Non-liftability of the Galois (abelianised) action into the normaliser of an inertia generator: the extension of γ_{ρ,σ} by {±1} pulled back from N*_ρ → N*_ρ/{±1} is non-trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction class in H^2(G, Z/2) for lifting a homomorphism through a central Z/2-extension; Galois action on normalisers of inertia subgroups in profinite π1
ideas.usually_credited_to: General framework standard; the Galois/GT action on inertia normalisers was studied by Ihara, Nakamura, Drinfeld and others
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; continuation of La Longue Marche material

ideas.what: Identifying the extension by a ladder of cartesian squares relating it to an extension M(0)^~ of a subgroup M(0) induced from S_0^πΓ^!.
ideas.modern_name: Pull-back of group extensions / cartesian diagram of μ-torsors

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step inside a long unpublished computation. It identifies a ±1 extension via standard pull-back diagrams. The specific claim (non-splitting of the sign in the normaliser action) is an internal detail, not a striking new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Equation label '(155)' (with '(152)' struck out) is presumably meant to be (145), consistent with (144) before and (146) on the next page.
The group written Γ_{ρ,σ} in the transcription appears in the image as a lowercase script γ_{ρ,σ}, consistent with the next page.
The diagonal element in (144) is S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} '(sans !)', mapping 'can (passage au quotient)' to γ_{ρ,σ}. The dashed inclusion goes from it to S_0^πΓ^!_{ρ,σ}.
